News and Insights
Blog

We dig deep every day inspiring each other to identify new perspectives and opportunities. Our team-based culture stimulates debate and promotes fresh ideas which can lead to real value for our clients.
We expect income growth to offset negative leverage and keep CRE market valuations roughly flat.

In a results-driven business, we believe building and maintaining relationships with broker-dealers is a key to success when trading on behalf of our clients, even for large and complex portfolio trades.
The US consumer remains resilient despite higher gas prices, a trend we expect to continue for the holiday season.
In our view, the concentration of investment growth in AI-related sectors is a concern, more so than the level of investment in the economy.
We maintain a constructive outlook for the CLO market, in particular investment grade-rated CLO debt.
European automakers face stiff competition in local markets from Chinese imports, contributing to our deteriorating fundamental outlook.
We believe several structural issues must be addressed before a meaningful rebound in Chinese consumption can take hold.

When analyzing a high yield data center construction project, the PPM credit team examines cash flow strength and associated risks: construction, tenant, lease cancellation and, finally, the structure of the bond itself.
Keiko Fujimori’s presidential election victory may usher in an era of political stability in Peru, providing meaningfully positive impacts on the country’s growth, confidence and asset performance.

With estimates of $3T in credit needed to fund AI-related projects through 2030, investors could benefit from partnering with an active manager that has experience of investing across all segments of the credit market, supported by an experienced and multi-skilled research team.

While tighter spreads in frontier markets imply less margin for error, we believe investors should still consider the asset class given its idiosyncratic nature and relatively wide spread dispersion compared to investment grade and other ‘core’ EM markets.
The potential bottoming out of the Chinese real estate market may have far-reaching impacts on the Metals & Mining and Luxury Retail sectors.
A recent industry conference reinforced overall consumer strength amid rising food and gas prices, but select sectors like packaged goods are more challenged.

We believe investors should consider allocating to EM debt for diversification given that EM economies currently have limited exposure to the AI investment cycle and could prove to be more resilient to potential AI labor shocks compared to the US.
As Investment Grade Private Credit grows, smaller club deals could offer investors greater pricing power and allocations.

On US trade with Mexico, we see meaningful guardrails against an “extreme” outcome given deep North American supply-chain integration. On security, however, the reaction function on both sides is less predictable, and the risk of unintended escalation may be higher.
